safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 4.0 days to 2.01 days

narrative: Material PL1__M017F74F exhibits regular, near-continuous daily demand averaging 453 units with a CV of 0.49, classifying it as normal-like in distribution. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.63, range 0.38–5.0 days), requiring a meaningful safety stock of 913 units to achieve 95% service level. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity (capped at 6,012 by storage capacity) reduces total annual cost by over 70% compared to the current MOQ-only SAP policy, while eliminating stockout exposure from the current zero-safety-stock baseline.
warnings: Storage capacity binding: safety_stock (913) + order_quantity (6012) = 6925, which equals max_storage_units (6925.46). No headroom remains for safety stock increases without reducing order quantity.
EOQ raw (9879) exceeds storage capacity and has been capped to 6012 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Regular, near-continuous demand with an unstable lead time distribution makes a continuous-review reorder-point model optimal. The EOQ minimizes the sum of ordering and holding costs; the safety stock covers stochastic lead-time demand at the 95% service level. The MOQ (1483) is non-binding since the EOQ-derived quantity (6012) exceeds it.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is essentially fully consumed by the recommended policy (913 + 6012 = 6925 vs cap of 6925.46). Any increase in safety stock—e.g., driven by increased lead time variability or higher service level targets—would require a proportional reduction in order quantity and a corresponding rise in ordering frequency and cost. This trade-off should be reviewed if demand or lead time conditions worsen.
